routes.name: Glacier Express route
routes.tagline: Zermatt to St. Moritz past the Matterhorn and over the Oberalp Pass
routes.blurb: These are real trains crossing the Alps right now, on the route of the Glacier Express.
stamps: Zermatt, at the foot of the 4,478 m peak
The Matterhorn's four faces point almost exactly north, south, east and west. It was first climbed in 1865.
Down from the Mattertal into the Rhône at Visp and Brig
The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier above Oberwald and flows through Lake Geneva all the way to the Mediterranean.
Dark larch-wood chalets along the upper Rhône
The Goms is the upper Rhône valley: a string of villages built from larch wood the sun has turned almost black, many of them centuries old.
Opened in 1982, the Furka Base Tunnel replaced the old summit line, which snow closed for much of every winter.
The crossroads of the Gotthard region
Andermatt sits where the routes to three passes meet: the Gotthard, the Furka and the Oberalp.
2,033 m, the highest point of the journey
The highest point of the journey. Lake Toma, a short walk from the pass, is often called the source of the Rhine.
A Benedictine monastery since the 8th century
The Benedictine abbey of Disentis was founded in the 8th century, and monks still live and teach there.
Almost 10,000 years ago a gigantic rockslide at Flims dammed the Rhine. The river has been cutting this gorge through the debris ever since.
People have lived at Chur for more than 5,000 years, which makes it one of the oldest towns in Switzerland.
65 m high, running straight into a tunnel in the cliff
Finished in 1902, the viaduct curves 65 m above the river and runs straight into a tunnel in the cliff face.
Loops and spiral tunnels climbing from Bergün to Preda
Between Bergün and Preda the line climbs about 400 m in 6.5 km as the crow flies, using 12 km of track, spiral tunnels and viaducts. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Journey's end in the Engadin, 1,775 m
St. Moritz has hosted the Winter Olympics twice, in 1928 and 1948.

routes.name: Bernina line
routes.tagline: St. Moritz to Tirano over the Bernina Pass and down to Italy
routes.blurb: These are real trains on the Bernina line right now, from the glaciers of the Engadin down to Italy.
stamps: One of the biggest glaciers in the eastern Alps
The glacier has retreated more than 2 km since the late 1800s. Signs along the path to it mark where its tongue reached in each decade.
Milky glacier water at the top of the line
The 'white lake' is a reservoir fed by glacier melt, which gives the water its pale green colour.
2,253 m, the highest point of the line
The highest railway crossing of the Alps. From here the line drops about 1,800 m to Tirano, without a single rack section.
A balcony above the Palü Glacier
Look down the valley: Poschiavo is about 1,000 m below, and the line zigzags all the way down to it.
Many grand houses here were built by local emigrants who made their fortunes as pastry cooks and café owners across Europe.
The line turns a full circle to lose height
With no room for a long ramp, the engineers looped the track over itself on a circular stone viaduct, completed in 1908.
The last stretch runs down the middle of the street, past the basilica square, into Italy.

routes.name: Gotthard panorama line
routes.tagline: Arth-Goldau to Bellinzona over the original 1882 Gotthard line
routes.blurb: These are real trains on the original Gotthard line right now, through the loops at Wassen and into Ticino.
stamps: The line hugs the shore of Lake Lucerne
This arm of Lake Lucerne is where, according to legend, William Tell leapt from his captors' boat to the shore.
The line loops around the village to gain height, so the little church appears below you, beside you and above you.
When it opened in 1882 it was the longest railway tunnel in the world. Around 200 workers died building it.
Out of the tunnel and into Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton. Even the light often feels different on this side.
Two helical tunnels let the line drop down a steep step in the valley, crossing over itself on the way.
Bellinzona's three medieval castles and its town walls are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
